subject: Acme - Pricing & Invoice Estimate & Cost Model
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alex Holmes <alex.holmes@acme.com>, Priya Ramesh <priya.r@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Acme discovery recap + next steps (pricing info we discussed)

Alex / Priya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can get you a clean invoice estimate + cost model: 

- Use case summary: in-app assistant for sales reps (short prompts + long context for some workflows).
- Initial traffic estimate: you mentioned 1–2M prompts/month across 2 products — can you confirm expected average tokens per prompt and any peak-day multipliers?
- Model mix: you said you want a higher-quality model for compose flows and a cost-optimized model for classification. Please confirm preferred model family (e.g., open-llama-65B quantized / redwood-7B or similar).
- Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to keep cloud inference spend around $X per 1M tokens. Can you provide a target $/1M tokens or an initial monthly budget range?

What we’ll send back after you confirm: a simple spreadsheet cost model (tokens/month breakouts), an invoice-style estimate PDF, and a short note on optimizations (batching, caching, model variant routing) that impact unit price.

Next steps: can you reply with – 1) expected avg tokens per prompt, 2) expected monthly token volume (or range), 3) target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range?

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa on shipping the model + invoice artifacts.
—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0118

[Attachment: none]

From: Alex Holmes <alex.holmes@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap + next steps (pricing info we discussed)

Thanks Sean — good meeting. Answers below: 

1) Avg tokens per prompt: ~650 tokens (average 450 input / 200 output), but compose flows can spike to ~2,500 tokens for multi-turn summaries.
2) Current month estimate: 12M tokens/month across both apps; 6–8M stable, ability to burst to ~30M on product launches. 12mo projection: 200M tokens/month if adoption ramps as expected.
3) Budget / target $: initial pilot budget $3k–$5k/month. For long-term, we’re looking for unit economics under $20 per 1M tokens (target) once we scale — upper bound comfortable at $40/1M for higher-quality model.

We need an invoice estimate for procurement to start the PO process; Priya is the procurement lead and will review the line items.

Alex
Alex Holmes
Head of Product — Acme Corp
alex.holmes@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

[Attachment: none]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alex Holmes <alex.holmes@acme.com>, Priya Ramesh <priya.r@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap + next steps (pricing info we discussed)

Alex / Priya — thanks for the details. Attached is a first-pass cost model and invoice-style estimate based on the ranges you gave. Highlights: 

- Base assumptions included in the spreadsheet: 650 avg tokens/prompt, 12M monthly tokens baseline, 30M burst, model mix: 70% redwood-7B (inference-optimized) + 30% redwood-70B-equivalent (higher-quality variant).
- Unit economics summary (ballpark): $18/1M tokens (weighted avg) at 12M/month with the model mix above; with caching and batching optimizations we can push below $15/1M in many workloads.
- Invoice estimate (PDF attached) shows monthly line items + one-time set-up. We included an option for dedicated reserved capacity (savings shown) versus on-demand.

Attachments: ACME_token_cost_model_20261019.xlsx (spreadsheet) — pricing-calculator-v2.xlsx (internal calculator used to generate the estimate) — redwood-invoice-estimate-20261019.pdf (invoice-style estimate)

Priya — can you confirm if procurement needs Net30, PO number style, or a DocuSign invoice to start? We can also break out the pricing by route (hosted vs dedicated) if you want a side-by-side.

If this looks good, we’ll prepare a formal quote and DocuSign envelope to lock prices for 30 days.

Thanks,
—Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com

[Attachment: ACME_token_cost_model_20261019.xlsx (spreadsheet); redwood-invoice-estimate-20261019.pdf (pdf); pricing-calculator-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet - internal)]

From: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Alex Holmes <alex.holmes@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap + next steps (pricing info we discussed)

Sean — thank you for the model and estimate. A couple quick clarifying questions before procurement signs off: 

- Tokenization assumptions: does the spreadsheet assume byte-pair encoding / specific tokenizer per model? We have some prompts with long embedded product specs; curious how that affects tokens counted.
- Caching/prefix savings: are the prefix caching estimates included in the baseline $/1M figure or listed as separate optimizations? If separate, can you show the delta for our 12M baseline?
- Line-item request: procurement needs a clear line for model inference cost, data-retention logs (if applicable), and any SLA/add-on fee.

If you can get back with those details in-line in the spreadsheet (or a short follow-up email), we can circulate to Finance. Also, procurement prefers a DocuSign-ready PDF for a pilot PO.

—Priya
Priya Ramesh
Procurement Lead | Acme Corp
priya.r@acme.com

[Attachment: none]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@acme.com>, Alex Holmes <alex.holmes@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap + next steps (pricing info we discussed)

Priya — great questions. Quick answers inline and attached updated artifacts: 

- Tokenization: spreadsheet uses the redwood tokenizer baseline (BPE) for the model family noted; we included a tab that counts tokens for several sample prompts including your long product-spec examples. I ran the spec through the tokenizer and it increased the per-prompt average to ~900 tokens for those cases — see tab "Spec-heavy prompts".
- Caching/prefix savings: baseline invoice assumes no prefix caching (conservative). We added an optional savings scenario in the spreadsheet that shows a ~12–22% reduction in effective tokens for typical shared prefix workflows; for your 12M baseline that translates to ~$2k–$3k/month savings in the mid case (see tab "Caching Scenarios").
- Line items: updated the PDF to include separate lines for: inference compute (per-1M token unit), data retention/logging surcharge (optional), premium SLA (optional), and one-time integration/onboarding fee.

Next steps: I attached an updated spreadsheet and a DocuSign-ready invoice PDF. If that looks good I can start the DocuSign flow and we can apply the pilot pricing for 30 days while you complete PO.

Attachments included: ACME_token_cost_model_20261019.xlsx (updated with tokenizer examples + caching scenarios); redwood-invoice-estimate-20261019.pdf (DocuSign-ready)

Would you like me to remove the dedicated capacity option from the invoice for now and send a version that only shows hosted on-demand pricing?

—Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com

[Attachment: ACME_token_cost_model_20261019.xlsx (updated); redwood-invoice-estimate-20261019.pdf (DocuSign-ready)]
